gloss: just when, on the verge of

definitions.gloss: just when, right when, at the very moment
definitions.explanation: A point in time just as something was about to happen or had just started. Typically followed by an unexpected or inconvenient event.

examples.japanese: {出|で}かけようとした{矢先|やさき}に{雨|あめ}が{降|ふ}り{出|だ}した。
examples.english: Just as I was about to leave, it started raining.

examples.japanese: {回復|かいふく}しかけた{矢先|やさき}に、また{熱|ねつ}が{出|で}た。
examples.english: Just when I was starting to recover, I got a fever again.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{仕事|しごと}に{慣|な}れてきた{矢先|やさき}に{転勤|てんきん}を{命|めい}じられて{途方|とほう}に{暮|く}れた。
examples.english: Just when I was getting used to my new job, I was ordered to transfer and felt completely lost.

notes:
USAGE:
Used in the pattern ～した{矢先|やさき}に or ～しようとした{矢先|やさき}に. The event that follows is almost always unexpected, inconvenient, or unfortunate. This creates a sense of bad timing or irony.

ETYMOLOGY:
{矢先|やさき} literally means "arrowhead" ({矢|や} = arrow, {先|さき} = tip). The metaphor suggests the precise point where the arrow is aimed — hence, the exact moment.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- ～した{矢先|やさき}に: just when ~ happened
- ～しようとした{矢先|やさき}に: just as ~ was about to ~
- ～(よ)うとしていた{矢先|やさき}: just as ~ was trying to ~
